newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee closes shade weaker vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee closes shade weaker vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee ended a shade weaker on Wednesday on limited speculative buying of dollars, dealers said.
It closed at 56.45 to the dollar after opening at 56.40.

"The amount of commercial demand was almost negligible. The upward movement was almost entirely on speculation that the Central Bank will continue to let the rupee fall," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The speculation was prompted after the Central Bank pushed down the rupee by only half a local cent in the morning despite the dollar's overnight dip against European currencies.
Dealers said the dollar did not rise further because the Federal Reserve signalled no change in U.S. interest rates.
Overnight call money closed at 13.5 percent after opening at 16, dealers said.
The rupee/dollar market will be closed on Thursday for a Buddhist holiday. It will reopen on Friday
